subject: Evening peak: intermittent stream slowdowns — Orchidai
content:
From: Amir Patel <amir@orchidai.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 20:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evening peak: intermittent stream slowdowns

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing intermittent stuttering / long pauses in streamed responses from the Redwood chat endpoint during our evening peak (approx 19:30–20:05 PT). The UI shows partial chunks and then long gaps (3–7s) before the next chunk arrives. This affected ~7% of requests across two regions (us-west-2, us-east-1).

We tested switching to non-streamed generation and response times looked normal. Attaching a tar of request traces and chunking logs (orchidai_stream_logs_20261028.tar.gz). Can you confirm if this matches anything on your side?

Thanks,
Amir
Amir Patel
Head of Platform — Orchidai

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Amir Patel <amir@orchidai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 20:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Evening peak: intermittent stream slowdowns

Hi Amir — thanks for the quick report and for the logs. We’ve started triage.

Immediate notes:
- Acknowledged impact window and observed symptom (partial chunks, 3–7s gaps).
- We’ve asked infra to pull edge- and shard-level telemetry for the same timeframe.
- Temporary mitigations we can try while we investigate: reduce client chunk size and enable our recommended soft-fallback. Details below.

Requested from Orchidai:
1) The client-side streaming config for the failing calls (chunk size, timeout per chunk, any retry settings).
2) A short HAR or network capture around a failing interaction, if possible.

Temporary mitigations you can try (low-risk):
- Set client header X-Redwood-Streaming-Chunk to 512 (was 1024) to reduce per-chunk processing.
- Add a 1.5s client-side chunk timeout and auto-retry the single chunk (this reduces perceived stall).
- If acceptable for the UX, fallback to non-streamed generation for the highest-concurrency endpoints until we close.

I’ll loop Marissa (runtime lead) and Karthik (platform) for deeper triage. We’ll follow up within 2 hours with an initial finding.

—
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, Amir Patel <amir@orchidai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 21:05:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Evening peak: intermittent stream slowdowns

Hi Amir — quick engineering note from runtime: we observed brief packetization stalls on a subset of edge nodes connected to the us-west-2 front door around 19:40 PT. Root cause appears to be a combination of an unusual tokenization distribution for Orchidai’s prompts (many short tokens then a long tail) plus a temporary kernel preemption on two GPU hosts serving the streaming variant.

Short-term actions we’re taking now:
- Rebalanced a small set of streams off the impacted edge nodes to mitigate immediate stalls (completed 19:58 PT).
- Increased downstream socket write buffer and disabled a non-critical preemption window that was coincidentally scheduled for that hour.

Client-side recommendations (safe to apply immediately):
- Reduce per-chunk byte size to 512 (header: X-Redwood-Streaming-Chunk: 512).
- If you use chunk-aggregation on ingest, set max_tokens_per_chunk to 32 for now.
- Add a simple client retry: if stream stalls >2.5s, retry the request as non-stream.

We’ll continue to look at kernel scheduling logs and quantization paths that could amplify packetization jitter for token distributions like yours. I’ll post an interim triage doc to the Jira link Jasmine included.

—
Marissa Cole
Runtime Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Amir Patel <amir@orchidai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evening peak: intermittent stream slowdowns — follow-up and postmortem link

Hi Amir — thanks again for the quick collaboration and for the traces you uploaded. Per Marissa’s triage and our infra investigation, the short summary:

What happened (high level):
- During the 19:30–20:05 PT window our edge-to-shard pipeline experienced transient packetization stalls on a small subset of nodes in us-west-2. Two GPU hosts serving the streaming variant had concurrent kernel schedule preemptions while processing an atypical tokenization profile from Orchidai’s prompts. The combined effect produced sporadic 3–7s gaps for ~6–8% of streams.

Why the workaround helped:
- Reducing chunk size and max_tokens_per_chunk reduces the per-chunk compute and I/O footprint, which reduces susceptibility to kernel preemption jitter.
- Client-side short retry for stalled chunks prevents the UX from blocking while the backend recovers.

Customer-facing one-paragraph you can share with PM/QA:
- On 2026-10-28 evening peak we observed intermittent pauses in streaming responses for a small fraction of requests. We deployed a temporary mitigation (rebalanced streams and kernel preemption window disabled) and recommend a short client-side change (reduce streaming chunk size to 512 bytes and a 2.5s stall retry). These mitigations reduce visible stalls while we complete a full postmortem and a longer-term runtime fix.

Next steps (our side):
- Postmortem published: https://drive.redwood.com/postmortems/orchidai-20261028-stream-slowdown.md (internal + shared read-only link for you).
- Engineering action items: scheduler hardening to avoid preemption at peak windows; improved tokenization-aware kernel selection; better edge-level automatic rebalancing. ETA: fixes and a staged rollout targeted by 2026-11-12.
- We will credit Orchidai for the incident: one week of host credits applied to your account; billing team will follow up separately.

If you want, I can join a 30-min sync with your PM/QA to walk through the short note and confirm the A/B test risk profile.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
